setlist_extra.title: The Music Never Stopped, Set Break

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Morning Dew** (6 reviews): Phil's bass in the solo is outstanding, and Brent's organ in the final build nearly drowns out Jerry; Reviewer calls it the best Morning Dew played in 1990 [20][22][23][24][26][28]
- **Friend Of The Devil** (1 review): Reviewer singles out Friend Of The Devil and Ramble On Rose as standouts [26]
- **The Music Never Stopped** (1 review): Me and My Uncle into Mexicali and Music Never Stopped are on the slow side, which reviewer likes [29]
- **Aiko Aiko** (1 review): Reviewer says Brent is tearing it up and urges listening to Aiko [29]

## The recordings

- **gd1990-03-18.mtx.hansokolow.96568.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 171 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]. Said about its sound: Shakedown sounds odd at the opening, but sound is fine by Stagger Lee [28]
- **gd90-03-18.sbd.huck.9364.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 169 min; rated 4/5 by 11 [2]. Said about its sound: Shakedown has odd sound problems at the start and in the middle; the rest of the recording is high quality; Shakedown has recording problems, but the rest of the soundboard is very good; Healy had trouble with the Shakedown sound and only fixed it by Stagger Lee [20][21][22][25][27]
- **gd1990-03-18.naks.andrewf.35401.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 23 songs; 163 min [3]
- **gd1990-03-18.149785.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 21 songs; 172 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [4]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says this was the first show of the 1990 Hartford run [22]
- Hartford was a hectic scene with tickets very hard to get; reviewer sneaked into one night [23]
- Reviewer's only Dead show; notes it was the second-to-last time the band played Hartford [24]
- The two-night run was the last at the downtown Hartford arena [27]
- Reviewer disputes that this is the best run of Spring 90, though both Hartford shows are worth hearing [25]
- Reviewer says the next night's unusual end-of-song Eyes jam is essential listening [25]
- Reviewer finds the two Hartford nights stronger than the Nassau shows, which sound somewhat over-produced [26]
- Reviewer calls this another epic Hartford Morning Dew, noting the band delivered it nearly every Hartford visit [29]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1990-03-18.mtx.hansokolow.96568.flac16**: transferred by hansokolow; source: Matrix mix (SBD/AUD) [1]. Also: Matrix by hansokolow in ProTools, blending the HCN soundboard feed from ISDN via master reel and DAT with audience splices; Audience source used Sennheiser ME-80 mics into a Technics SV-MD1 DAT, first row, on Maxell tapes [1]
- **gd90-03-18.sbd.huck.9364.sbeok.shnf**: source: Hartford Civic Center SBD feed to HCN studios via ISDN > HCN Master Reel > DAT(Sony ES)recorded/(Tascam DA20mkII) playback>Pioneer PDR 555>CDR>WAV>SHN [2]
- **gd1990-03-18.naks.andrewf.35401.flac16**: taped by Andrew F; transferred by Andrew F; source: Nakamichi CM-300's with CP-4 shotgun capsules > Sony TC-D5M > Maxell MX-90 cassettes, with no Dolby. Mics on stand 7-feet high, set up near the back of the… [3]. Also: Audience taping and transfer by Andrew F.; tape flip between discs two and three loses under five seconds [3]
- **gd1990-03-18.149785.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  April 7, 2020; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-X90) [4]. Also: Charlie Miller's ultramatrix from pre-FM reel master; Drums from 4:45 onward come from the shnid 9364 DAT source [4]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1990-03-18 Grateful Dead Backstage Pass - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1990-03-18-grateful-dead-backstage-pass/) [32]
- Photo by a Flickr member (All rights reserved): [Grateful Dead - 3/18/90 Civic Center, Hartford, …](https://www.flickr.com/photos/104729480@N03/27287244252/) [33]
- Photo by uncredited: [the page](https://www.flickr.com/photos/104729480@N03/27287244252/) [34]
